name: Kitchen Layout Updates: How to Plan Appliance Clearances and Walkways

step.name: Step 1: Document existing structural boundaries and mechanical rough-ins
step.text: Measure every wall length, ceiling height, window opening, and doorway, noting the exact locations of supply pipes, drains, gas pipes, electrical panels, and vent exhausts. Take photos of where mechanical chases run so you know what can move easily and what will drive up structural framing or sub-trade expenses.

step.name: Step 2: Confirm exact appliance specification sheets before drawing cabinetry
step.text: Collect the manufacturer cut sheets for your chosen range, refrigerator, dishwasher, and microwave drawer. Verify both the exterior unit dimensions and the open-door swing depths to make sure your proposed aisles will not be blocked when loading or unloading.

step.name: Step 3: Lay out primary work aisles and dedicated clearance zones
step.text: Map out your walkways to ensure at least a 42-inch clearance for single-cook spaces or 48 inches if multiple people prep food together, with clear 36-inch paths for general home traffic. Reserve at least 30 by 48 inches of unobstructed floor space directly in front of each major appliance.

step.name: Step 4: Check drawer runs and door swings against adjoining cabinet faces
step.text: Plot corner cabinets, pull-out spice racks, and full-extension drawers to ensure hardware or handles do not collide when opened simultaneously. Incorporate proper filler widths between cabinet boxes and adjacent drywall so doors open past 90 degrees without scraping trim.

step.name: Step 5: Assemble drawing sets and coordinate local permit approvals
step.text: Combine your architectural cabinet elevations, structural adjustments, and mechanical trade drawings into a unified permit package for review by local municipal building officials before purchasing materials.
